markets.caveat: listed survivors only; dead tokens and exchanges absent
14:15 CET accounting fixing, NOT a tradable quote; no spread, no carry, no intraday
implied volatility LEVELS, not option prices. Any P&L derived from these is modelled, not observed.

strategies.title: Low-Volatility Tilt
strategies.description: Long the calmest quintile of the liquid US universe, short the wildest, rebalanced monthly. The low-volatility anomaly is among the most replicated effects in equities: high-beta, high-variance names persistently underperform on a risk-adjusted basis.
strategies.caveat: Survivorship works AGAINST this one. Failed high-volatility names are missing from the data, which should make the short leg look better than reality, not worse.

strategies.title: 12-1 Momentum
strategies.description: Long the strongest decile by return over the last twelve months excluding the most recent one, short the weakest, held a month. Skipping the recent month avoids short-term reversal, which is a different and opposing effect.
strategies.caveat: Momentum crashes. The worst months for this strategy cluster in sharp market rebounds, and a three-year sample may not contain one.

strategies.title: Low-Vol + Momentum Blend
strategies.description: The average of the two rank signals above. They are close to uncorrelated -- one prefers calm names, the other strong ones -- so blending should raise the ratio of signal to idiosyncratic noise without adding a new hypothesis.
strategies.caveat: A blend of two things measured on the same data is not a third independent piece of evidence.

strategies.title: Crypto Trend Following
strategies.description: Hold each coin only while it trades above its own 100-day average, equal-weighted across whichever qualify, otherwise sit in cash. Time-series momentum is the single most documented effect in crypto and the one most consistent with how the asset class actually moves.
strategies.caveat: Survivorship is severe here: dead tokens and failed exchanges are simply absent, and total loss is a normal outcome in this market rather than a rare one.

strategies.title: Crypto Cross-Sectional Momentum
strategies.description: Long the third of coins with the strongest 30-day return, short the weakest third, rebalanced weekly. Tests whether relative strength within crypto predicts, separately from the market's own direction.
strategies.caveat: A dollar-neutral crypto book still carries large residual risk: these assets correlate near one in a sell-off, which is exactly when the hedge is needed.

strategies.title: FX Trend Following
strategies.description: Long the third of currencies with the strongest 60-day trend against the dollar, short the weakest third, rebalanced monthly. Trend following in currencies is the oldest systematic strategy there is and the basis of most managed-futures programmes.
strategies.caveat: ECB reference rates are a daily accounting fixing, not a tradable quote. There is no spread here and no interest-rate carry, and carry is where much of the real return in FX actually lives.

strategies.title: FX Mean Reversion
strategies.description: The opposite bet at a shorter horizon: short whichever currencies rose most over five days, long those that fell most, held a week. Currencies are widely held to overshoot at short horizons and trend at long ones, so this and the trend strategy above should not both work.
strategies.caveat: Same fixing caveat as above. If both this and FX trend show a profit on the same data, suspect the data before believing both.

strategies.title: Short Volatility / Theta Decay
strategies.description: Sell a one-month at-the-money straddle on the index every month and hold it to expiry. The position profits whenever the index moves less than the implied volatility it was sold at, which is usually: the variance risk premium is one of the most persistent effects in derivatives.
strategies.caveat: MODELLED, not backtested. P&L is computed from VIX against realised SPY movement; no free chain data exists, so bid-ask, skew and assignment are assumed rather than observed.

strategies.title: Iron Condor (monthly, 1-sigma wings)
strategies.description: Sell a one-month iron condor with short strikes one standard deviation out and defined-risk wings beyond them. Keeps the whole credit whenever the index finishes inside the wings, which on a one-sigma band is most months, and loses a capped amount when it does not.
strategies.caveat: MODELLED, not backtested. Worse than the straddle: a condor's P&L depends on the volatility SMILE, and VIX is a single number that contains no skew at all.

strategies.title: Variance Premium, Regime-Timed
strategies.description: The same short straddle, opened only when implied volatility sits above its own trailing one-year median. The gap between implied and realised is widest when volatility is already elevated, so standing aside in calm regimes avoids collecting almost nothing for the same tail risk.
strategies.caveat: MODELLED, not backtested. It also adds a timing rule to a strategy already in this table, which is one more hypothesis tested on the same data.
